decisions.question: Decided by the maintainer on 2026-10-31, walked through with session -81. Reopen condition (4), a count of replica-set sites, was dropped because a replica set is optional, so the event's source is the write's own result. (1) Scope: an in-process event, with records named from the write step's WriteResult.items[]. It is complete because every supported write goes through Nightscout (direct writers to MongoDB are unsupported; xDrip+'s MongoDB upload is deprecated). Delivery between processes is decided with the serve roles. A timer runs only for time-driven alarms, never to catch up on writes. The event stays internal and unstable until a subscriber outside lib/ exists. (2) Two events: one per write(intent), equal to its WriteResult, for subscribers; and the per-database-call event kept as backend instrumentation for differential analysis across backends, which is not a contract. (3) Each record entry carries _id, identifier, outcome, and the problems list for refused records, plus collection, source and counts. There are no document contents and no filter. Above the 1,000 cap the event lists no records and says so, and readers reload. Under multitenancy each event also carries the tenant. (4) It ships with write(intent) release 2, aimed at 16.0.0 through the entry bar (nothing is ruled out of 16.0.0). Subscribers are added as each clears its gates: the one-person profile's alarm check, then the cache, then the socket's dataUpdate. Follow-up, separate: the CLI pattern for roles under each tenancy (nightscout single [roles,...] vs nightscout multitenant [roles,...]). The aim is one theory of operations for single-tenant and multitenant sites, since a single-tenant site already runs a headless API v3, with the monolithic single-tenant site staying the default (see D-EXEC-PROFILE).

options.label: Per-write event from items[], in-process; per-call kept as instrumentation
options.gains: exact on every site with no extra read (release 2 already resolves ids); one fact per write that a later transport can carry; backend comparison through the per-call event
options.risks: delivery between processes is still to be decided with the serve roles

decisions.owner: maintainer; framed 2026-10-31, evidence from the profile prototype
decisions.question: Tenancy (one site's data or many) and execution (a resident ddata kept current, or views computed from bounded queries when a write, a timer or a request needs them) are separate axes. Today the subcommand couples them: single is one tenant with a resident ddata; the explicit multitenant API preview now builds request-local loader frames. Evaluator/realtime and the separate computed-profile prototype remain distinct work. A third profile, one tenant computed on demand, would let an independent or low-cost single-tenant site skip the resident ddata without taking on multitenancy or PostgreSQL. It also takes the alarm trigger inside one process, so it does not wait on a cross-process change feed. single keeps its resident path either way. Execution mode is chosen by evidence (maintainer, 2026-10-31): "If the evidence suggested that single tenant needs ddata for cost savings/freemium quotas, then we need to keep that behavior as appropriate." Evidence needed: alarm and properties equality through the profile's own trigger (replay lab, the execution plan §7b cases), and per-tenant memory, CPU per evaluation, database operations per write and per tick, idle cost, and the latest-reading latency, resident against computed, at the full windows the views need (60 h treatments, 24 h device statuses), giving the break-even between the two. Roles are a third axis (maintainer, 2026-10-31, follow-up open): a single-tenant site already runs a headless API v3, so `nightscout single [roles,...]` beside `nightscout multitenant [roles,...]` would give single-tenant and multitenant sites one theory of operations, with the monolithic single-tenant site staying the default.

options.label: Prototype and measure, then choose per profile
options.gains: the execution mode is picked from measured cost and equality; the same views serve single-tenant and multitenant hosting
options.risks: a third start profile to document and test

options.label: Keep the coupling: single resident, serve computed
options.risks: a single-tenant site that would be cheaper without a resident ddata cannot have it

options.label: Make computed the only execution mode
options.risks: loses the resident cache where it is the cheaper one (a site that is viewed constantly); single's behaviour changes

The maintainer decided 2026-10-29 to proceed without waiting, revisable when Loop answers: (1) identifier format: 1 to 256 URL-safe characters, a UUID recommended, placeholders (invalid, undefined, null, NaN) refused; (2) _id: a client may still send an ObjectId _id over API v1 (legacy); going forward the server sets _id and the client sets identifier.
